new.name: Grant Harland Muse Jr.
new.description:
Grant Harland Muse Jr., a thirty-five-year-old Episcopal priest at Good Shepherd Church in Berkeley, rode the Illinois Central Railroad from New Orleans to Jackson, Mississippi, and was arrested on June 20, 1961, for participating in the Freedom Rides — one of the arrests recorded by the Mississippi State Sovereignty Commission and preserved in the Civil Rights Digital Library. The catalog establishes the arrest, the participation, and the individually identified police photograph, but not the court disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the physical release date; those fields are unresolved pending county-jail, court, or penitentiary records.

His birth year, about 1925, is an estimate from his reported age at arrest; no exact birth date has been located.

updates.append: The catalog in fact preserves two distinct arrest records for Wahlstrom, then a twenty-two-year-old University of Wisconsin psychology student: the June 6, 1961 arrest at the Jackson Trailways terminal after riding from New Orleans with six other Freedom Riders, and a second arrest at the Jackson Greyhound terminal on July 31, 1961, during another Freedom Ride. His birth year, about 1938, is an estimate from his reported age; both custody outcomes remain unresolved.
